title: Zhoug Chicken Shawarma Bowls
blurb: Charred, spice-lacquered shawarma thighs piled over lemony cucumber-tomato salad with garlicky green zhoug yogurt.

ingredients.item: 1 cup Friendly Farms plain whole-milk Greek yogurt
1 English cucumber, cut into small dice
1/2 small red onion, sliced paper thin
1 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves, roughly chopped
1 tsp sumac or Chili Lime Seasoning
Olive oil, kosher salt, black pepper

steps.text: Set a cast iron or heavy stainless skillet over medium-high and let it preheat dry for a full 2 minutes, until a flicked drop of water skitters instead of sitting still. Pat the thighs dry with paper towels while it heats.
steps.tip: A wet thigh steams; a dry one chars.

steps.text: Add a slick of olive oil, then lay the thighs down in a single layer with space between them. Sear undisturbed until the underside is deep mahogany and the edges have crisped, about 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Crowding the pan kills the crust.

steps.text: Flip and cook another 5 minutes, until the thickest part is opaque all the way through and the juices run clear. While it cooks, dice the cucumber and tomatoes.
Toss the cucumber, tomato, red onion, and parsley with the juice of half the lemon, a glug of olive oil, salt, and plenty of black pepper. Taste it — it should be aggressively lemony.
Stir the zhoug into the Greek yogurt with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of the remaining lemon until it turns pale green and pourable.
steps.tip: Thin with a splash of water if it's too stiff to drizzle.

steps.text: Move the chicken to a cutting board and rest it for 5 minutes, then slice across the grain into thick strips. Meanwhile, blister the naan directly in the hot skillet, about 1 minute per side.
steps.tip: Resting keeps the juices in the meat.

steps.text: Smear hummus across the bottom of two shallow bowls, then heap on the salad and the sliced chicken. Drizzle the zhoug yogurt over everything and dust with sumac.

swap: If the marinated shawarma thighs are gone, use plain Kirkwood chicken thighs rubbed with 21 Seasoning Salute, cumin, and paprika.
leftovers: Keep chicken and salad in separate containers up to 3 days and rebuild as a wrap in an L'Oven Fresh Protein Wrap with hummus.

title: Bahian Shrimp Moqueca
blurb: Sweet Argentinian red shrimp poached in a coconut-lime broth stained sunset orange with paprika and fire-roasted peppers.

ingredients.item: 1 lb Raw Argentinian Red Shrimp, thawed and peeled
2 cups frozen Fire Roasted Peppers & Onions
2 servings Frozen Jasmine Rice or Earthly Grains rice pouches
Olive oil, kosher salt, black pepper

steps.text: Toss the shrimp with the juice of one lime, a big pinch of salt, and black pepper. Let them sit while you build the base.
steps.tip: A quick lime cure firms up the shrimp.

steps.text: Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat, then add the sliced onion with a pinch of salt. Cook until soft, floppy, and translucent at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, paprika, and tomato paste and stir constantly for 1 minute, until the paste darkens to brick red and the pan smells toasty rather than raw.
steps.tip: Raw tomato paste tastes tinny — cook it out.

steps.text: Pour in the coconut milk and the frozen peppers and onions, scraping the bottom of the pan. Simmer over medium-low for 10 minutes, until the broth thickens slightly and orange fat pools at the edges.
steps.tip: Heat the rice while this reduces.

steps.text: Slide the shrimp into the broth in a single layer and poach gently for 3 minutes, spooning liquid over the tops, until they turn opaque and curl into loose C shapes.
steps.tip: Tight O shapes mean they went too far.

steps.text: Kill the heat and stir in most of the cilantro, the Chili Lime Seasoning, and the juice of the second lime. Taste and add salt until the coconut sweetness snaps into focus.
Spoon the moqueca over hot jasmine rice in wide bowls and finish with the remaining cilantro and a lime wedge.

swap: Any bag of frozen raw shrimp works; if peppers and onions are out, use a sliced red bell pepper cooked with the onion.
leftovers: Refrigerate up to 2 days and reheat gently over low heat so the shrimp don't seize; it makes an excellent sauce for rice noodles.

title: Mamak-Style Mee Goreng with Shrimp and Egg
blurb: Blistered noodles tangled in a sweet-hot chili gravy with seared shrimp, soft egg curds, and a hard squeeze of lime.

ingredients.item: 8 oz Fusia rice noodles or thick egg noodles
12 oz raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
4 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt

steps.text: Boil the noodles one minute shy of the package time so they still have spring, then drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with a teaspoon of oil so they don't fuse.
steps.tip: Undercook them — they finish in the pan.

steps.text: Whisk the sweet chili sauce, soy sauce, ketchup, and sriracha together in a small bowl. This is your gravy, and having it premixed is the whole trick to a fast stir-fry.
Heat your largest skillet over high until a bead of oil shimmers and just barely wisps smoke. Pour in the eggs and scramble hard for 1 minute into big soft curds, then scrape them onto a plate.
Add another splash of oil and lay the shrimp down in one layer. Sear about 1 minute per side, until pink and opaque at the edges, then move them to the plate with the eggs.
steps.tip: They will finish cooking when everything comes back together.

steps.text: Toss in the garlic and cabbage and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the cabbage wilts at the edges but the ribs still crunch.
Add the drained noodles and all of the gravy, then toss with tongs for 2 minutes, letting the noodles sit still for a few seconds at a time so they catch color against the hot metal.
steps.tip: Stillness is where the smoky wok flavor comes from.

steps.text: Fold the shrimp, egg, and scallions back in and turn off the heat. Squeeze the lime over the top and finish with spoonfuls of Crunchy Chili Onion.

swap: Fusia gyoza, pan-fried and sliced, can stand in for the shrimp if the seafood case is picked over.
leftovers: Best eaten immediately, but leftovers revive in a hot dry skillet with a splash of water rather than the microwave.

title: Persian Lemon-Turmeric Chicken and Chickpea Khoresh
blurb: A golden, sour-savory stew of fall-apart chicken, chickpeas, and jammy caramelized onion, flooded with lemon at the end.

ingredients.item: 1 cup Friendly Farms Greek yogurt, for serving

steps.text: Pat the thighs very dry and season them hard with salt and pepper on both sides. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high until it shimmers and thins out.
Brown the chicken in two batches, about 4 minutes per side, until the surface is deep gold and the pieces release from the pot without sticking.
steps.tip: If a thigh grips the pan, it isn't browned yet.

steps.text: Move the chicken to a plate and add the onions with a big pinch of salt. Cook over medium for 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping up the browned bits, until they collapse into a deep gold jam.
steps.tip: Juice the lemons and drain the chickpeas while this happens.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric, cinnamon, and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, until the whole pot smells toasted and the paste turns brick colored.
Return the chicken and any juices, then add the broth and chickpeas. Bring to a bare simmer, cover, and cook for 30 minutes, until the meat pulls away from the bone under gentle fork pressure.
steps.tip: Bubbles should barely break the surface.

steps.text: Uncover, stir in the lemon juice and cranberries, and simmer 10 minutes more so the liquid tightens around the chickpeas and the cranberries plump.
Shred the chicken right in the pot with two forks and fish out the bones. Taste and push it further with salt and more lemon until it tastes bright, not muddy.
steps.tip: Persian stews should land sour first, rich second.

steps.text: Heat the basmati and serve the khoresh ladled over it, showered with parsley and finished with a cold spoonful of yogurt.

swap: Boneless thighs work fine — cut the covered simmer to 20 minutes; dried apricots can replace the cranberries.
leftovers: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two; freeze in portions and reheat with a splash of broth to loosen.

title: Skirt Steak with Hand-Chopped Chimichurri
blurb: A hard-seared, deeply crusted steak sliced thin under a raw, vinegary flood of parsley, garlic, and oregano.

ingredients.item: Specially Selected olive oil, kosher salt, black pepper

steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°F and salt the steak generously on both sides, then leave it on the counter to take the chill off while everything else comes together.
steps.tip: Salt early so it has time to penetrate.

steps.text: Toss the halved potatoes with olive oil and salt, spread them cut-side down on a sheet pan, and roast for 20 minutes until the cut faces are crisp and deep gold.
steps.tip: Cut-side down is what builds the crust.

steps.text: While they roast, finely chop the parsley, garlic, and shallot by hand and stir them together with the vinegar, oregano, pepper flakes, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup olive oil.
steps.tip: A blender turns chimichurri into sad green paste.

steps.text: Let the chimichurri sit for 10 minutes so the garlic mellows and the oregano rehydrates. Taste it — it should be sharp enough to make you blink.
Set a cast iron skillet over high heat for 4 minutes, until it is faintly smoking and the surface looks dull rather than shiny.
Pat the steak bone dry, oil it lightly, and lay it down. Sear for 3 minutes without touching it at all, until a dark, continuous crust forms.
steps.tip: Every peek costs you crust.

steps.text: Flip and sear 3 minutes more for medium-rare — the center should feel like the fleshy pad below your thumb when pressed.
Rest the steak on a board for 8 minutes, then find the direction of the muscle fibers and slice thin straight across them.
steps.tip: Cutting with the grain makes skirt steak chewy.

steps.text: Dress the arugula with lemon, olive oil, and salt. Plate the steak, spoon chimichurri over it generously, and add the potatoes with the chimichurri hot sauce alongside.

swap: Carne Asada Autentica from the meat case works beautifully here and skips the seasoning step entirely.
leftovers: Store sliced steak submerged in leftover chimichurri for up to 3 days; it is excellent cold in a sandwich on Specially Selected brioche buns.

title: Crispy General Tso's Chicken and Broccoli
blurb: Shatter-crisp cornstarch-coated chicken tossed at the last second in a glossy, chile-flecked sweet-savory glaze.

ingredients.item: 1 lb Simply Nature Organic Chicken Breasts, cut in 1-inch cubes
1 large head broccoli, cut into small florets
6 dried red chiles or 1 tsp red pepper flakes

steps.text: Toss the chicken cubes with the egg white and 1/2 teaspoon salt, then add the cornstarch and toss again until every piece looks chalky and dry with no wet patches left.
steps.tip: The dry cornstarch shell is what shatters.

steps.text: Pour 1/2 inch of neutral oil into a skillet and heat over medium-high for about 4 minutes, until a dropped scrap of coating sizzles vigorously on contact.
Fry the chicken in two batches for about 4 minutes each, turning once, until pale gold and firm to the touch. Drain on a rack, not paper, so the bottoms stay crisp.
steps.tip: Two batches keeps the oil hot enough to crisp.

steps.text: While the second batch fries, steam or microwave the broccoli for 3 minutes until it turns vivid green and a fork meets slight resistance.
Pour off all but a tablespoon of oil, drop the heat to medium, and add the garlic, ginger, and chiles. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant and just barely blond — never browned.
steps.tip: Burnt garlic will ruin the whole sauce.

steps.text: Pour in the General Tso's sauce and soy sauce and let it bubble for 2 minutes, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Kill the heat, add the chicken and broccoli, and toss fast for about 30 seconds so everything is glazed but the crust hasn't had time to go soggy.
steps.tip: Sauce it at the last possible second.

steps.text: Heat the jasmine rice and serve immediately, scattered with scallions and sesame seeds.

swap: Fusia sweet and sour sauce makes a great milder version; Season's Choice frozen broccoli florets save you the knife work.
leftovers: Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat in a 400°F oven or air fryer for 6 minutes to bring the coating partway back.

title: Doro Wat-Style Chicken with Jammy Eggs
blurb: Chicken braised down into a dark, buttery red onion sauce lit up with harissa and cardamom, with soft-yolked eggs sunk in at the end.

steps.text: Put the diced red onions in a wide skillet over medium heat with no fat at all and cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until they release their water, collapse, and turn sticky.
steps.tip: The dry start is what makes doro wat taste like doro wat.

steps.text: Meanwhile, lower the eggs into boiling water and cook exactly 7 minutes for jammy centers, then shock them in ice water and peel.
Add the butter to the onions and let it foam, then stir in the harissa, paprika, cardamom, ginger, and garlic. Cook 2 minutes until the mixture darkens to a glossy brick paste.
Cut the chicken into large chunks, season with salt, and fold it into the paste until every piece is coated red.
Pour in the broth, bring to a low simmer, and cook partly covered for 20 minutes, until the chicken shreds under a fork and the sauce has reduced to something that clings rather than pools.
steps.tip: Stir once or twice so the bottom doesn't catch.

steps.text: Score the peeled eggs lightly all over with a knife tip and nestle them into the sauce, spooning it over the tops. Simmer 3 minutes to warm them through.
steps.tip: Scoring lets the sauce soak into the whites.

steps.text: Finish with a squeeze of lemon and salt to taste, then warm the naan in a dry pan for about 1 minute per side until it puffs and spots.
Serve straight from the skillet with torn naan as the scoop — this is a dish meant to be eaten with your hands.

swap: Zhoug Sauce plus an extra teaspoon of paprika can replace the harissa; bone-in thighs work with 10 extra minutes of simmering.
leftovers: Keeps 3 days and deepens overnight; reheat low and slow, adding a splash of broth, and top with a fresh egg.

title: Tex-Mex Beef and Black Bean Chili with Unexpected Cheddar
blurb: A thick, cumin-heavy chili built on hard-browned grass-fed beef and fire-roasted salsa, buried under sharp crumbly cheddar.

ingredients.item: 2 lb Simply Nature Organic Grass-Fed Ground Beef
2 cans black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high for 2 minutes, then add half the beef and press it into a flat slab. Leave it completely undisturbed for 4 minutes so a genuine brown crust forms.
steps.tip: Crowded beef steams gray and tastes like nothing.

steps.text: Break the slab into chunks and cook 3 more minutes until no pink remains, then move it to a bowl with its juices and repeat with the second half.
Add the onion and bell pepper to the rendered fat and cook over medium for 8 minutes, until softened with browned edges. Drain and rinse the beans while you wait.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, and tomato paste and keep it moving for 2 minutes, until the spices smell toasted and the paste darkens against the pot.
steps.tip: Blooming the spices in fat doubles their punch.

steps.text: Return all the beef, then add the salsa, crushed tomatoes, black beans, broth, and a teaspoon of salt. Scrape every browned bit off the bottom as it comes up to heat.
Bring to a simmer, drop to low, and cook uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a trail that closes slowly.
steps.tip: If it thickens too fast, add broth a splash at a time.

steps.text: Taste and correct: more salt if it tastes flat, more chili powder if it tastes sweet, a pinch more cumin if it tastes thin.
Pull it off the heat and let it rest 10 minutes to set up, then ladle into bowls and bury each one under a mound of grated Unexpected Cheddar.
steps.tip: Grate the cheddar cold — it crumbles rather than smears.

swap: Never Any! ground turkey or chorizo can stand in for the beef; pinto or kidney beans work as well as black.
leftovers: Holds 5 days refrigerated and freezes for months; spoon it over Casa Mamita tortilla chips with more cheddar for nachos, or into warm tortillas.
